items.title: GitLab Dedicated: A go-live guide
items.summary: GitLab Dedicated is a single-tenant SaaS solution that is fully isolated, deployed in your preferred AWS cloud region, and hosted and maintained by GitLab. GitLab Dedicated and compliance covers why regulated organizations choose a single-tenant instance operated by GitLab, and serves as a starting point for evaluation. In this article, you'll learn what to do after you sign on to GitLab Dedicated, including understanding which responsibilities GitLab takes on and which remain with your teams, as well as what controls each team needs to put in place.Teams arriving from any self-managed source-control or CI/CD platform bring an operating model built around upgrade runbooks, pre-flight checks, staging environments, and rollback plans. On GitLab Dedicated, many of those responsibilities move to GitLab, and the ones that stay with you look different.Division of responsibilityGitLab Dedicated splits platform operation between GitLab and the customer.GitLab ownsYou ownVersion validation and testingPipeline configurationSecurity patchingScripts and services calling the GitLab APIDatabase migrationsWebhooks and integrationsMonitoring and observabilityRunner configurationBackup and regional recoveryMigration away from deprecated featuresThe right-hand column is where most of your team's work now sits. GitLab operates the platform. Your teams operate what runs on it.What you configure in SwitchboardSwitchboard is the administration portal for GitLab Dedicated. From there, you manage:IP allowlists for inbound accessSAML and instance authenticationOperational email addressesAccess to your application logs, which GitLab delivers to a private Amazon S3 bucketAWS PrivateLink connections and bring-your-own-key encryptionHosted runnersSwitchboard has two roles: Admin edits instance configuration and manages Switchboard users; Read-only views instance data.Some capabilities must be enabled on your tenant by GitLab before they appear in Switchboard. If an option you expect is missing, contact your Customer Success Manager or Support before troubleshooting permissions.GitLab Dedicated does not provide shell access to the infrastructure, feature flags, experimental features, or modified GitLab source. These constraints are what allow GitLab to carry the availability SLA and keep every instance on the supported upgrade path.How upgrades workGitLab Dedicated runs one minor version behind current GitLab, a model known as N-1. Your instance has a weekly maintenance window, chosen at onboarding. Most weeks that window carries patches and infrastructure work. Once a month, after each GitLab release, it carries the minor version upgrade. Each release has already run on GitLab.com before it reaches your instance.Major versions arrive roughly once a year. Breaking changes are announced in the deprecations list in advance, typically with at least a month's notice. GitLab also identifies customers using features scheduled to change and contacts them ahead of the upgrade.Upgrade validationGitLab SREs validate each release against internal test environments before it reaches any customer instance. The pre- and post-upgrade health checks documented for GitLab Self-Managed don't apply to Dedicated, because they require infrastructure access that customers don't have. GitLab monitors your instance and contacts you if an upgrade causes a problem.For teams used to running their own upgrade validation, this is the biggest change in the operating model. Upgrade testing moves from your team to GitLab's.Maintenance windows and exceptionsYour maintenance window cannot be changed after onboarding. Two things can move an upgrade off your window:Production change locks are declared by GitLab during periods of reduced GitLab staffing, such as major holidays. They pause all production changes, including Switchboard configuration. An upgrade due during a lock moves to the first window after it lifts. You can’t request a lock for your own change freeze.Emergency maintenance covers urgent actions such as a platform outage, serious degradation, or a critical security fix. It’s applied outside your window and can’t be postponed.For emergency security patches, GitLab withholds vulnerability details until disclosure because publishing early would expose customers that have not yet been patched. Details are published through the vulnerability disclosure process 90 days after release.Reference architecture changes happen when your instance needs resizing, for example to support more load. GitLab schedules the change with you in advance. During the resize, content stays readable, but most writes, including Git pushes, fail and new CI/CD jobs don’t start. Plan for up to an hour per size step.RollbackVersion rollback is not part of the GitLab Dedicated operating model. It is also not a supported operation on GitLab Self-Managed.
